articles.title: Global Energy Import Dependence Set to Peak by 2034, Rystad Says
articles.description: Rystad Energy’s fifth edition of its flagship annual report, Global Energy Scenarios (GES) 2026, finds that global reliance on imported energy is projected to peak by 2034 as energy security concerns accelerate the shift towards electrification. Against the backdrop of two major energy crises in five years, the report highlights how a broader range of rapidly deployable technologies is helping the energy system withstand major disruptions to energy flows. It explores how energy import dependency could evolve under three possible future scenarios,…

articles.description: Energy data provider TGS has agreed terms with PetroGuin to secure the rights to reprocess the JAAN 3D seismic dataset across Guinea-Bissau on a multi-client basis.

articles.title: USA Crude Oil Stocks Drop Almost 9MM Barrels WoW
articles.description: Commercial crude oil stocks, not including the SPR, came in at 415.577 million barrels on October 9, the EIA's latest weekly petroleum status report revealed.

articles.title: Norway's Untapped Oil and Gas Frontier Is Drawing Renewed Interest
articles.description: More than three decades after Norway opened parts of the Norwegian Sea to petroleum exploration, potentially significant oil and gas resources remain hidden beneath thick layers of volcanic rock. Now, advances in exploration technology and renewed industry interest could bring one of Europe's least explored offshore frontiers back into focus. Norway may still hold substantial undiscovered oil and gas resources in areas that have remained virtually untouched by exploration drilling for more than 30 years. According to the Norwegian Offshore Directorate,…

articles.title: U.S. Offers Another 17 Million SPR Barrels as Fuel Crisis Deepens
articles.description: The United States is putting another 17 million barrels of crude from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve on offer, one day after the IEA accelerated emergency stock releases as governments scramble to get more oil and fuel into a tight market. The Department of Energy issued a request for proposals Friday for an exchange of up to 17 million barrels, part of the 172 million barrels Washington committed to make available under the IEA’s 400-million-barrel emergency action announced in March. The SPR currently holds about 283 million barrels. If…

articles.title: Wind Farm Approved in Victoria, Australia Would Be Largest in Southern Hemispher
articles.description: A massive wind farm in the state of Victoria, Australia, has been approved by state authorities, paving the way for the project to go to the federal environment minister for final checks. ABC News reports Planning Minister Sonya Kilkenny this week signed off on the Warracknabeal Energy Park, five months after its environmental impact report was approved. WestWind Energy plans to build 219 turbines and install two 300-megawatt battery energy storage systems across 26,000 hectares of farmland in the heart of Victoria’s wheat belt. The site…

articles.title: U.S. Oil Drillers Back Off Even As Prices Soar
articles.description: The total number of active drilling rigs for oil and gas in the United States remained unchanged this week, according to new data that Baker Hughes published on Friday, with the total rig count in the US staying at 603, up 55 from this same time last year. The number of active oil rigs fell by 3, to 459 during the latest reporting period, according to the data. This is 41 above this same time last year. The number of gas rigs rose by 1 to 133, which is 12 more than this time last year. Miscellaneous rigs rose by 2 to 11. The latest EIA data showed…

articles.title: Equatorial Guinea Rewrites Oil Law After Production Collapses 85%
articles.description: Equatorial Guinea will approve a new hydrocarbon law on Monday after crude production collapsed to just 20,000 barrels per day in September, down from roughly 140,000 bpd in 2020. The 120,000-bpd loss has reduced OPEC’s smallest producer to a fraction of its former output and contributed to an economy the International Monetary Fund expects to shrink 1.7% this year. Hydrocarbons Minister Antonio Oburu Ondo said the new law will make contractual terms more flexible and offer oil companies a wider range of structures based on their appetite…

articles.title: Oil Prices Are Stuck at $105 as Geopolitical Risks Mount
articles.description: Brent holds near $105 as Iranian tanker attacks and multiple geopolitical conflicts keep oil markets on edge. October 16, 2026 Oil prices have been relatively rangebound this week as the current modus operandi of frequent Hormuz transits and frequent Iranian drone attacks found an equilibrium point around $105 per barrel for ICE Brent. Production shut-ins triggered by Hurricane Isaias no longer provide bullish support as total offline capacity in the US Gulf of Mexico dipped to 200,000 b/d by Friday, with offshore production returned to its pre-Isaias…

articles.title: IMF Sounds Alarm Over AI’s Threat to Government Tax Bases
articles.description: The head of the International Monetary Fund has warned financial ministers that widespread AI adoption could erode tax bases across the world as incomes are squeezed by the technology. Kristalina Georgieva, the managing director of the IMF, said governments may be ill-prepared for a potential slump in tax revenue brought on by AI’s impact on the labour market. At the fund’s summit in Bangkok, Georgieva has issued a series of warnings on the impact of AI, calling the technology a “slow-moving tsunami” that could affect…

articles.title: German Power Supply Startups Exit Market as Wholesale Prices Soar
articles.description: Two startup electricity retailers in Germany have recently announced they would cease operations as spiking wholesale prices amid the gas price surge are pressuring the industry again, and this time the pressure is compounded by plans for renewable policy changes. Renewable electricity provider Grüüün, part of Münch Energie Group, early this month said it would discontinue servicing about 200,000 residential customers as of October 31, 2026, and these will now have to switch to other providers. articles.description: BW Energy has announced that recent appraisal drilling on the Dussafu field offshore Gabon has identified commercial oil volumes, with an estimated combined gross recovery of approximately 8-9 million barrels (mbbl).

articles.title: Global Gas Crunch Makes Europe’s Remaining Coal Plants Profitable
articles.description: The global LNG supply crunch has made Europe’s last-standing coal-fired power plants profitable this year as gas supply costs soar while the need for conventional generation to stabilize grids remains. In Germany and Poland, which host most of the remaining operational or back-up-ready coal power capacity in Europe, coal-fired generation is profitable again as winter approaches, LNG supply is barely moving out of the Strait of Hormuz, and gas prices are at their highest level since the 2022-2023 crisis. articles.title: Ukraine Defies Trump With Renewed Attacks on Russian Oil Infrastructure
articles.description: Ukrainian forces have struck an oil refinery in Russia's Ryazan region, Russian officials said, hours after President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine would resume attacks on Russian energy facilities and voiced anger over a "dangerous" disruption of satellite intelligence from the United States. Defying an "energy cease-fire" announced unilaterally last week by US President Donald Trump, Zelenskyy told the Financial Times in an interview published on October 15 that "we're done" with holding off on launching attacks on Russia's oil structures.…

articles.description: The trading arm of China’s state-owned giant PetroChina is set to reap a record more than $3 billion (20 billion yuan) in trading profits this year as the Middle East crisis hiked crude prices and rattled global fuel markets and trade flows. PetroChina International (PCI), the trading vehicle of the biggest oil and gas producer in Asia, is set to book more than $3 billion in gross trading profit for 2026, anonymous trade sources told Reuters.
